High Courts operate at state level

items: Crucial distinction: High Court judges are appointed by the President, but their oath is taken before the Governor.
The retirement age for High Court judges is 62 years.
High Courts have the authority to issue writs for enforcement of legal rights and exercise administrative control over subordinate courts.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: High Courts function as the primary judicial bodies at the state level.
The mandatory retirement age for High Court judges is 62 years.
Judges of the High Court are appointed directly by the President of India.
The oath of office for High Court judges is administered by the State Governor.
High Courts possess writ jurisdiction for legal rights and hold supervisory control over subordinate courts.
